body.message:
# Proposed decomposition — PRD 002

_Open questions resolved by adopting all documented defaults (single-slot untitled session store; curated pinnable cosmetic subset; separate recent caps; greyed unavailable-folder root; config-dir-only global admin file)._

---

## Parent issue (never labeled `Sandcastle`)

**Title:** Workspaces & layered configuration

**Body:**

> **[decomposer · claude-code · claude-opus-4-8]**
>
> Replaces Marky Mark's flat, single-scope `settings.json` model with (1) a four-layer configuration resolver — **Global < Team < Workspace < User** — where per-setting scope tags decide which layer wins, and (2) VS Code-style **workspaces** that bundle multiple folder roots plus workspace-scoped settings into one portable `.marky-workspace` JSON file. Adds the File-menu flows (Open Folder / Open Workspace / Add Folder / Save Workspace As / Close Workspace / Open Recent), a multi-root sidebar, and a Settings UI with User | Workspace tabs showing effective values and overrides. Cloud/team sync is out of scope but the Team layer's slot and precedence are reserved for it. Desktop-only feature; web keeps the same resolver over Global < Team < User.
>
> **PRD:** prd/002-workspaces-and-layered-configuration.md

---

## Child issues (all labeled `Sandcastle`)

### Child 1 — Layered configuration resolver, scope tags & settings inventory
_Blocked by: none (foundation)_

Acceptance criteria:
- Every setting resolves through four ordered layers **Global → Team → Workspace → User**; the highest layer that provides a value wins (§A1).
- Each setting carries exactly one scope tag with documented precedence — **U** (settable anywhere as default, User wins), **U!** (User-layer only, ignored elsewhere — `author`), **W** (Global/Team/Workspace may set, User value ignored — `commentStorage`, `imageFolder`, `imageNamePattern`), **M** (never in the layered merge) (§A2, §B5).
- Resolution is pure/deterministic given the four layer inputs; unit tests cover each scope tag's precedence and the **W** and **U!** exclusion rules (§A3).
- Unknown/malformed keys in any layer fall back to the next layer down and ultimately baked defaults, matching today's tolerant `parseSettings` (§A4).
- Layer sources wired: **Global** = `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` + optional `<configDir>/global-settings.json` (absent by default); **Team** = reserved slot honored if present; **User** = existing `<configDir>/settings.json` (§F21).
- Resolver, scope tags and layer contract are shaped so a future Team layer / cloud-sourced Global/Workspace layers plug in without changing precedence semantics (§I27).

### Child 2 — Workspace model, `.marky-workspace` file, session state & migration
_Blocked by: Child 1_

Acceptance criteria:
- Three workspace states — **no workspace**, **untitled workspace**, **named workspace** — with at most one current at a time (§C7).
- Opening a folder creates an untitled workspace with that folder; adding a folder makes it a multi-root untitled workspace (§C8).
- `.marky-workspace` is pretty-printed **JSON** with a schema/version marker, an ordered list of folder references, and workspace-scoped settings (W + pinned cosmetic defaults); it contains **no** M-scoped/session state (§C9).
- Folder references stored relative to the workspace file where possible, resolved to absolute at load; unreachable folders surfaced (greyed) rather than dropped silently (§C10).
- Untitled-workspace state autosaved to a single current-untitled slot under `<configDir>/session/`, surviving restart until Save Workspace As (§C11).
- A named workspace autosaves folder-membership and workspace-settings changes back to its file — no explicit Save Workspace command (§C12).
- Folder root(s) + open-tab/expanded/active-file state become **per-workspace** machine-local session state; switching workspaces restores that workspace's own tabs and expanded tree (§B6, §F22).
- The current workspace is reopened at launch, consistent with today's reopen-last behavior (§C13).
- Migration is non-destructive and silent: existing `settings.json` is read unchanged as the **User** layer (no keys moved/lost, no prompt); an existing single `foldertree.json` root is adopted as an untitled workspace with one folder on first launch, rewriting nothing (§G23, §G24).

### Child 3 — File menu, workspace flows & multi-root sidebar
_Blocked by: Child 2_

Acceptance criteria:
- File menu provides **New**, **Open…** (file), **Open Folder…** (untitled workspace), **Open Workspace…**, **Open Recent ▸**, **Add Folder to Workspace…**, **Save Workspace As…**, **Close Workspace**, then the existing Save / Save As / Export / Print / Close Window items, grouped with separators (§D14).
- **Open Recent** lists recent workspaces first, a separator, then recent files, then Clear Menu — MRU, deduped, separate cap per section, corruption-tolerant, disambiguated labels (§D15).
- **Close Workspace** returns the app to the no-workspace state (empty sidebar), leaving any open single file as-is (§D16).
- The folder sidebar renders multiple roots when a workspace has >1 folder, each root independently expandable, reusing the existing lazy folder-tree behavior per root (§D17).

### Child 4 — Settings UI: User | Workspace tabs with override indicators
_Blocked by: Child 1, Child 2_

Acceptance criteria:
- Settings window gains a **User | Workspace** scope selector; the User tab shows all settings and writes the User layer; the Workspace tab is enabled only when a workspace is open, shows only workspace-eligible settings (W + a curated pinnable cosmetic subset), and writes to the `.marky-workspace` file (or the untitled workspace session store) (§E18).
- Each row shows the **effective value** and, when a higher-precedence layer overrides the tab's own layer, an indicator naming the winning layer (e.g. "overridden by User"); W settings shown on the User tab are indicated as workspace-controlled and not user-editable (§E19).
- Global and Team layers are read-only in the UI (no editing controls) but their resolved contributions are reflected in effective values/indicators (§E20).

### Child 5 — Platform boundary: desktop-only workspace features & web resolver parity
_Blocked by: Child 3, Child 4_

Acceptance criteria:
- Workspace features (Open/Save/Add Folder/Close Workspace, the multi-root sidebar, the Workspace settings tab) are **desktop-only**; the web build shows none of them (§H25).
- The same resolver runs everywhere; on web the effective config is **Global < Team < User** (no Workspace layer), so the future cloud/web multi-user version is an extension, not a rewrite (§H26).

---

**Dependency summary:** 1 → 2 → 3; 2 → 4 (and 1 → 4); 3 & 4 → 5.

Reply `APPROVED` to create this tree, or send feedback to revise.
